description: Sends a short briefing message ~60 minutes before each external calendar event. Polls every 15 minutes via launchd, reads the Calendar Sync local cache, looks up Contacts memory for each attendee, and delivers the brief via `openclaw message send`. Dedupes via a sent-briefs log so each event is briefed at most once.
name: Pre-Meeting Brief

app_dependencies.reason: Pre-Meeting Brief reads upcoming events from memory/calendar-upcoming.json (the schema Calendar Sync writes). Without Calendar Sync there is no event source, so the brief has nothing to fire on.

If Contacts is installed, the brief includes a 'Context' block per attendee drawn from memory/contacts/{slug}.md (commitments + recent notes). Without Contacts the brief simply lists attendees without per-person context.

integrations.reason: Calendar Sync (the upstream app) authenticates against Google Calendar. Pre-Meeting Brief reads its cache, so the underlying integration must be present.

alternatives.reason: Path-C service-account auth from PR #1862. Same scope requirement passes through to this app via Calendar Sync.

messaging_channel.reason: Delivers each pre-meeting brief to the operator's primary channel via `openclaw message send`.

data_files.description: Bounded log of event IDs that have already had a brief sent. Used for dedup across the 15-minute polling cadence so each event is briefed at most once.

schema.storage_format: JSON array of objects, capped at 200 entries (oldest pruned)

fields.sent_at: ISO datetime with offset — when the brief was sent
fields.event_start_iso: ISO datetime with offset — for audit and retention pruning

identity.purpose: Reduce 'walked into meeting cold' as a failure mode. About an hour before each external calendar meeting, deliver a short brief naming the meeting, listing attendees, and pasting in any per-person context the operator has already captured in the Contacts memory layer. The brief is a pure read+compose+send — it never touches the calendar itself.
scope_includes: Run on a 15-minute launchd polling cadence
Read upcoming events from memory/calendar-upcoming.json (written by the Calendar Sync app)
Filter events whose start falls within the configured lookahead window (default 45–75 minutes from now) AND have at least one external attendee (is_external==true)
For each qualifying event not yet in the sent log, compose a brief including title, time, attendees, and per-attendee context from memory/contacts/ if Contacts is installed
Send the brief via `openclaw message send` to the user's recorded channel
Append to memory/pre-meeting-sent.json with the event_id so the next 15-minute poll skips it
Support `--dry-run` for poll (compose + print + skip send + skip log write)
Emit PREMEET_SENT: / PREMEET_FAILED: / PREMEET_SKIPPED: signals for the delivery monitor
scope_excludes: Reading the Google Calendar API directly — the Calendar Sync app owns auth and event fetching
Internal-only meetings (all attendees in the bot's primary domain) — these are skipped on purpose
Sending RSVPs, declines, or any write to the calendar
Sending briefs to attendees — delivery is only to the operator's primary channel
Multi-brief escalation (no 'second reminder 10 minutes before' — one brief per event)
Recurring meeting deduplication based on series — each instance gets its own brief if its event_id is unique
identity.bot_interaction_pattern: Cron-driven daemon at 15-minute cadence. The bot is not invoked as a session — launchd runs the script directly, which delivers via `openclaw message send`. The bot can also be asked 'preview my next pre-meeting brief' in conversation, which runs the preview-next subcommand.
identity.user: The primary bot operator. Briefs go to the operator's primary channel only — never to meeting attendees.

observable_outcomes: When an external meeting is scheduled within 45–75 minutes from now, a brief arrives in the primary channel within one 15-minute poll cycle
Each event is briefed exactly once — memory/pre-meeting-sent.json gains exactly one entry per event_id
Attendee context is populated when memory/contacts/{slug}.md exists for that attendee, and absent otherwise (no fabrication)
Internal-only meetings (is_external==false) emit PREMEET_SKIPPED: internal_only and do not surface to the operator
If memory/calendar-upcoming.json is missing or empty, the poll exits 0 silently — no false PREMEET_FAILED:
failure_signals: External meeting starts and no brief was sent in the prior hour — daemon not running or window logic broken
Same event briefed twice in one day — sent-log dedup not honored
Brief sent for an internal-only meeting — is_external misread
Brief contains attendee context that contradicts what's in memory/contacts/{slug}.md — file read drift
Plist loaded but no PREMEET_SENT: signals for 24+ hours despite external meetings on the calendar — silent failure

quality_bar.minimum: External meetings produce a brief that names the title, time, attendees, and any contact memory the operator already has. Internal meetings are never briefed. Dedup prevents repeat briefs.
quality_bar.excellent: Briefs arrive on a consistent cadence (~60 min before start) regardless of when the event was added to the calendar. Context blocks are concise — only the most recent / most relevant items per contact. Operator never thinks 'I would have wanted that brief earlier' or 'why did I get this twice'.

privacy: Attendee email addresses and event titles are sensitive — briefs go only to the primary channel, never to logs or shared locations

Per-attendee context pulled from memory/contacts/{slug}.md may include private notes — the brief excerpts at most ~10 lines per contact and never quotes a contact's struck-through (completed) commitments
memory/pre-meeting-sent.json stores event_id + sent_at only, never event title or attendee list
safety: Read-only against the calendar cache and Contacts files — no writes to memory/calendar-* or memory/contacts/
Delivery send must time out within 60 seconds; on failure emit PREMEET_FAILED: and exit non-zero so the next poll can retry the event
If Calendar Sync's cache is older than 2 hours, log a warning to stderr but still process its contents (do not block on staleness)
dependencies: Calendar Sync (p-fe9acef3) — REQUIRED. Writes memory/calendar-upcoming.json. This app reads it.
Contacts (p-4136a932) — OPTIONAL. If memory/contacts/ exists, per-attendee context is included.
openclaw CLI — REQUIRED. Brief is delivered via `openclaw message send`.
boundaries: Polling cadence is fixed at 15 minutes — operator can change it by editing the plist's StartInterval; the script does not auto-adjust
One brief per event_id, ever. If a poll's sent log shows the event_id, skip — even across daemon restarts
Window is hard-coded to lookahead minutes from configuration; events outside the window are skipped, not queued
Brief never mentions internal attendees by name (privacy reflex even though it's only sent to the operator)

build_spec:
# Pre-Meeting Brief — Build Specification

## Overview

A launchd-driven script that polls every 15 minutes, reads the Calendar Sync local cache, and sends a brief ~60 minutes before each external meeting via `openclaw message send`. Dedup is via a bounded sent-briefs log.

No external API calls — all data is sourced from local files written by the Calendar Sync and Contacts apps.

**Prerequisite:** Calendar Sync (p-fe9acef3) must already be installed — `memory/calendar-upcoming.json` is the event source. Verify the file is readable before iterating events.

**Optional:** Contacts (p-4136a932). If `memory/contacts/` exists, attendee context is folded in.

## Python invocation

Use `python3` (let the deploy environment resolve the binary). Do not hardcode venv paths.

## File layout

```
scripts/
  pre_meeting_brief.py        ← main CLI (subcommands: poll | preview-next | status)
  pre-meeting-cron.sh         ← launchd trigger (rendered below)
memory/
  pre-meeting-sent.json       ← bounded sent-briefs log (created on first send)
```

## scripts/pre_meeting_brief.py

### Subcommands

```
pre_meeting_brief.py poll          --bot BOT_ID [--dry-run]
pre_meeting_brief.py preview-next  --bot BOT_ID
pre_meeting_brief.py status
```

- `poll` — scan upcoming events, brief any that qualify and haven't been briefed yet, update sent log, emit signals.
- `preview-next` — find the next external event within the next 24 hours, compose its brief, print to stdout. Does not send, does not update log.
- `status` — summarize memory/pre-meeting-sent.json (count, last 5 sent_at + event_id).

### Reading calendar cache

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
import json

def load_upcoming(workspace: Path) -> list[dict]:
    cache = workspace / "memory" / "calendar-upcoming.json"
    if not cache.exists():
        return []
    try:
        events = json.loads(cache.read_text())
        return events if isinstance(events, list) else []
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
        return []
```

### Window selection

From the configured `lookahead_minutes` (default 60, configurable in network.json), build the window:

```python
def in_window(event: dict, now: datetime, lookahead_min: int) -> bool:
    try:
        start = datetime.fromisoformat(event["start_iso"])
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False
    if start.tzinfo is None:
        start = start.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    # Lookahead window: events starting within [lookahead_min - 15, lookahead_min + 15] from now
    # (the +/-15 absorbs the 15-min polling cadence so each event gets briefed by the closest poll).
    delta_min = (start - now).total_seconds() / 60
    return lookahead_min - 15 <= delta_min <= lookahead_min + 15
```

### External-meeting filter

```python
def is_external(event: dict) -> bool:
    # Calendar Sync precomputes the is_external flag; trust it.
    return bool(event.get("is_external", False))
```

If the flag is absent, fall back to comparing attendee domains against the bot's primary email domain (from openclaw.json → email). If the bot's domain is unknown, treat the event as external (fail open — better to brief than to silently skip).

### Sent-briefs log

```python
def load_sent(workspace: Path) -> list[dict]:
    log_path = workspace / "memory" / "pre-meeting-sent.json"
    if not log_path.exists():
        return []
    try:
        data = json.loads(log_path.read_text())
        return data if isinstance(data, list) else []
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
        return []

def append_sent(workspace: Path, event_id: str, event_start_iso: str) -> None:
    log_path = workspace / "memory" / "pre-meeting-sent.json"
    sent = load_sent(workspace)
    sent.append({
        "event_id": event_id,
        "sent_at": datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(),
        "event_start_iso": event_start_iso,
    })
    # Bound the log: keep last 200 entries
    sent = sent[-200:]
    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Atomic write
    import os, tempfile
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=log_path.parent, suffix=".tmp")
    with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
        json.dump(sent, f, indent=2)
    os.replace(tmp, log_path)
```

Dedup check is by event_id: if any entry in `sent` has the same event_id, skip with `PREMEET_SKIPPED: {event_id} already_sent`.

### Per-attendee context lookup

```python
def contact_context(workspace: Path, email: str, max_lines: int = 8) -> list[str]:
    name_part = email.split("@")[0].lower().replace(".", "-")
    contact_file = workspace / "memory" / "contacts" / f"{name_part}.md"
    if not contact_file.exists():
        return []
    try:
        text = contact_file.read_text()
    except OSError:
        return []
    # Pull the Commitments section's first N non-empty, non-completed lines
    lines = []
    in_section = False
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if line.startswith("## "):
            in_section = line == "## Commitments"
            continue
        if not in_section or not line:
            continue
        # Skip struck-through (completed) commitments: lines containing ~~text~~
        if "~~" in line:
            continue
        lines.append(line)
        if len(lines) >= max_lines:
            break
    return lines
```

The slug rule mirrors Contacts: `email.split('@')[0].lower().replace('.', '-')`. The slug rule used here MUST stay in sync with whatever Contacts uses; if Contacts changes its slug computation, update this script to match.

### Brief composition

```python
def compose_brief(event: dict, workspace: Path) -> str:
    title = event.get("title", "Untitled meeting")
    start_iso = event.get("start_iso", "")
    try:
        start_local = datetime.fromisoformat(start_iso).astimezone()
        when = start_local.strftime("%-I:%M %p %Z")
    except ValueError:
        when = start_iso
    attendees = event.get("attendees", []) or []
    lines = [
        f"Meeting in about 60 minutes: {title}",
        f"  Start: {when}",
    ]
    if attendees:
        lines.append(f"  Attendees: {', '.join(attendees)}")
    lines.append("")
    # Per-attendee context
    any_context = False
    for email in attendees:
        ctx = contact_context(workspace, email)
        if ctx:
            any_context = True
            lines.append(f"Context for {email}:")
            for c in ctx:
                lines.append(f"  {c}")
            lines.append("")
    if not any_context and attendees:
        lines.append("(No contact memory on file for these attendees.)")
        lines.append("")
    description = (event.get("description") or "").strip()
    if description:
        lines.append("Notes from event:")
        lines.append("  " + description[:240] + ("..." if len(description) > 240 else ""))
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n"
```

### Delivery

Same pattern as Evening Sweep / Morning Brief — reuse the canonical delivery pattern (docs/spec-gallery-delivery-convention-2026-06-11.md; reference implementation in docs/reference/capabilities/template/scripts/example_script.py): resolve (channel, target) from the pod network.json — which lives ONLY at the canonical shared path `/Users/Shared/evolve/network.json` (read it there; it is NOT at `/Users/<bot>/.openclaw/network.json` and NOT in the workspace — copy the `SHARED_DIR = Path('/Users/Shared/evolve')` constant and `load_network()` helper from docs/reference/capabilities/template/scripts/example_script.py verbatim) — reading `bots.<bot_id>.primary_user.external_ids` (channel priority: telegram, whatsapp, signal, imessage, slack, discord, sms, matrix — intersected with the bot's own enabled channels from its openclaw.json `channels.<name>.enabled`, falling back to the best recorded id when there is no overlap so the send fails loudly), then run `openclaw message send --channel=<ch> --target=<target> --message=<text> --json` as the bot user (binary: `shutil.which("openclaw")`, falling back to /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin; cwd = the executing account's pwd-database home, NOT $HOME, so node can resolve its CWD even under sudo-without--H; child PATH prefixed with the CLI's own bin dir so the `#!/usr/bin/env node` entrypoint resolves under launchd's minimal PATH; timeout 60s). Exit code 0 = the channel accepted the send. Never read gateway port/token; never POST to the gateway. On any send failure: emit `PREMEET_FAILED: {event_id} {reason}` and exit 2 — the next poll cycle will reattempt because the sent log only updates on a successful send. If the bot has no recorded delivery route: emit `PREMEET_SKIPPED: no-delivery-route` and exit 0 without marking any event as briefed.

### Configuration (network.json)

```json
"capabilities": {
  "pre_meeting_brief": {
    "enabled": true,
    "lookahead_minutes": 60,
    "channel": "primary"
  }
}
```

Defaults if absent: lookahead_minutes=60, channel=primary.

## scripts/pre-meeting-cron.sh

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# pre-meeting-cron.sh — 15-minute polling trigger.
WORKSPACE="/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace"
exec python3 "$WORKSPACE/scripts/pre_meeting_brief.py" poll --bot "{bot_id}" \
  >> "/tmp/{bot_id}-pre-meeting.log" 2>&1
```

## Test surface

```bash
python3 -m py_compile scripts/pre_meeting_brief.py
python3 scripts/pre_meeting_brief.py status
# Expected: prints 'No briefs sent yet.' on a fresh install
python3 scripts/pre_meeting_brief.py preview-next --bot {bot_id}
# Expected: prints next external event brief OR 'No upcoming external meetings.' if calendar empty
python3 scripts/pre_meeting_brief.py poll --bot {bot_id} --dry-run
# Expected: simulates a poll, prints briefs that WOULD be sent, does NOT update sent log
```

## Provenance marker

```python
# evolve: pkg=p-2c7a9b6e file=f-XXXXXXXX@<version>
```

## What NOT to include

- No direct Google Calendar API calls — Calendar Sync owns that.
- No HEARTBEAT.md sections.
- No openclaw.json mutation.
- No background daemons or sleep loops — launchd is the only scheduler.
- No retry-with-sleep on transient gateway failure — let the next 15-minute poll reattempt.

scheduled_actions.summary: Poll the calendar cache every 15 minutes; send a brief ~60 min before each external meeting (window: 45–75 min). delivered evidence is scheduler_state: briefs are conditional on upcoming meetings, so 'the poll ran' is the strongest deterministic delivery proof; the sent-log dedup owns per-event delivery. heal:none — a missed tick is covered by the next tick.

usage.how_to_use: The launchd poll handles delivery automatically. Use `preview-next` to see what the next brief would look like off-cycle. `status` reports the most recent deliveries.
